label: rem:strand-twist-datum-remark
title: Properties of the per-strand framing datum and the hypercharge candidate
html:
The per-strand framing datum is not a reading of the ribbon structure. In a ribbon category the twist \theta is determined by the braiding rather than freely assigned, and on the n-th Jones–Wenzl idempotent e_n it acts by the scalar (-1)^n A^{n(n+2)} [habiro2000], whose exponent is the Casimir n(n+2) of the colour. A ribbon twist therefore admits no free per-strand integer, and t is an addition to the structure, not a reading of it.

Three properties of the per-strand framing datum are proved. The residual S_n strand-relabelling action of the gauge groupoid preserves both T(t) and the full multiset \{t_1, \dots, t_n\}, so the datum descends to the horizontal (S_n, fixed-n) orbits. It is not yet known to descend to the vertical direction: stabilisation \beta \in B_n \mapsto \beta\sigma_n^{\pm 1} \in B_{n+1} adds a strand, hence a new entry t_{n+1}, and generically changes both the multiset and T(t). Since the writhe fails at exactly this move (proved in the Lean library), and the point of this datum is to supply what the writhe cannot, the vertical behaviour is the property most worth establishing — it is untested here. As with Q and I_3, the working convention evaluates the datum on the canonical Gröbner–Shirshov word at the tower's minimal level, where only the horizontal action survives. The bar involution (orientation reversal, the conjugate state) negates the datum, T(\bar t) = -T(t), so conjugate states carry opposite twist. Finally, T separates states at fixed writhe: over any fixed braid word — hence any fixed w — there exist framings with distinct total twist. The hypercharge conjecture requires exactly such a coordinate, since its factorization criterion shows any hypercharge invariant must separate a writhe-degenerate pair and no function of w can. The separation is a property of the free label. It is not a property of the ambient ribbon twist, which is constant on a fixed object by the paragraph above, so a candidate resting on it inherits the freedom of the label rather than the rigidity of the category. Supplying a separating coordinate is a necessary condition on the candidate, not evidence that the separation is physical.

The normalised candidate pairs the datum with the derived isospin: with Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = T(t)/3 (the colour-tube charge quantum of the quark picture, the helon-model normalisation [bilson-thompson2005], where the twist encodes the electric charge and the hypercharge is not encoded; the braided-ribbon-graph successor identifies twist with a U(1) charge conserved under the evolution moves [bilsonthompson2007, §V]) and I_3 the writhe-derived isospin, the candidate hypercharge is Y_t = 2\,(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3). This makes the Gell-Mann–Nishijima relation hold by construction if and only if the two independent charge routes agree, Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q against the crossing-derived Coulomb charge — a falsifiable consistency between framing and crossing data, not a definition. That consistency, together with the first-generation spectrum and its \mathbb{Z}_6 compatibility [baez-huerta2010], is the battery any candidate must pass before wiring; it is exactly the open content of the hypercharge conjecture, and no numerical claim is made here.
